nodes.label: Transparent WebP camera cutout for hero foreground delivery
nodes.rationale: WebP delivery version of the transparent camera cutout, 1254x1254 RGBA with alpha bbox (0,3)-(1240,1254). It shows a professional cinema camera rig and tripod isolated on alpha, tightly framed with the tripod legs cropped at the bottom, lit with dark cinematic onyx/blue-slate tones and restrained crimson reflections. It is the compressed counterpart of camera-reference-cutout.png: same pixel dimensions and alpha, about 232 KB versus 1.29 MB. The file is preloaded and used as the homepage hero foreground while remaining the swap point for a future 3D model.

nodes.label: Professional cinema camera rig subject
nodes.rationale: The opaque silhouette and documented extraction brief identify a professional cinema camera body with attached rig hardware rather than a generic consumer camera. The rig is the sole foreground subject and carries the original pose, perspective, proportions and mechanical detail from the Avaris hero reference.

nodes.label: Large square matte box with raised top flap
nodes.rationale: A broad square matte box dominates the left-center of the silhouette, with a raised upper flap visible in the alpha outline. The extraction prompt explicitly calls for the matte box and flap; WebP compression softens the finest edge details but preserves the overall shape.

nodes.label: Lens with subtle crimson reflection
nodes.rationale: A small cluster of red-dominant, burgundy-toned pixels within the dark lens/body area supports the documented crimson reflection. The exact glass highlight is a fine detail and is partly softened by lossy WebP delivery.

nodes.label: Upper monitor, top handle, rails and follow-focus hardware
nodes.rationale: The upper rectangular block and narrow attached forms correspond to the mounted monitor, top handle and small rig hardware named in the provenance prompt, including rails and follow-focus controls. Their precise mechanical identities are inferred from the silhouette plus the extraction brief.

nodes.label: Fluid head and bottom-cropped tripod legs
nodes.rationale: Below the body, the silhouette narrows to a central support and then spreads into multiple legs that continue to the bottom alpha edge. This matches the documented fluid head and tripod legs cropped by the original reference frame.

nodes.label: Three-quarter front-left camera orientation (uncertain)
nodes.rationale: The provenance prompt describes the camera body as a three-quarter view facing front-left, but the downsampled silhouette alone does not make that precise viewing angle unambiguous. Marked uncertain rather than asserted from visual reading.

nodes.label: True-alpha isolated cutout with no scene background
nodes.rationale: The WebP retains RGBA transparency: roughly 52.4 percent of pixels are fully transparent and 44.9 percent near-opaque, with alpha identical to the PNG. Background, ribbons, floor, haze, text, logo, navbar, checkerboard and cast shadow are absent, leaving clean edges for compositing.

nodes.label: Dark cinematic studio lighting on matte black hardware
nodes.rationale: Dominant near-black and blue-slate pixel values, sparse silver highlights and small burgundy/crimson accents preserve the original restrained cinematic lighting. The materials read as matte black camera body and metal rig hardware, not a brightly relit product shot.

nodes.label: Tight square composition with bottom-cropped legs
nodes.rationale: The square 1254x1254 canvas frames the rig tightly, with a small transparent margin at the top, monitor and matte-box tips included, and tripod legs intentionally cut by the bottom edge. This preserves the approved reference framing for bottom-aligned hero placement.

nodes.label: Homepage hero foreground and future 3D swap point
nodes.rationale: HeroCamera.tsx renders this WebP as img.camera-cutout with accessible alt text and marks it as the foreground replacement point for a finished GLB scene. README.md describes the desktop placement at 64.5 percent viewport height, bottom-aligned and centered at 47.7 percent viewport width.

nodes.label: Compressed counterpart of the PNG camera cutout
nodes.rationale: scripts/asset-provenance.json records camera-reference-cutout.png as the generated output and camera-reference-cutout.webp as its delivery format. Pixel comparison shows identical dimensions and alpha, near-identical RGB (mean channel differences about 0.8-1.0), and a file-size reduction from 1,293,254 to 232,198 bytes.

nodes.label: High-priority preloaded WebP delivery asset
nodes.rationale: index.html preloads the WebP with as=image and fetchpriority=high, and HeroCamera.tsx sets fetchPriority=high with async decoding. The compressed WebP is therefore the performance-oriented network delivery form of the larger PNG master.
